https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/09/05/vlag.text: Menü Kereső Kedves szavakkal simogatták egymást Putyin és Trump küldöttei, egyelőre eredmény nélkül Külföld A találkozóról készült sajtófotó – Fotó: Gavriil Grigorov / Sputnik / Pool / Reuters Molnár Zoltán Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Vlagyimir Putyin orosz elnök jelezte, nagyra értékeli Steven Whitkoff és Jared Kushner amerikai küldöttek közvetítését az orosz-ukrán háborúban – írta az orosz Interfax hírügynökség az amerikai-orosz találkozóról. Putyin kijelentette: „Itt természetesen nagyon fontos a közvetítés minősége, ahogy a bizalom is azok közt, akik ezt teszik.” Az orosz elnök szerint jól tudnak együttműködni, magasfokú a kölcsönös bizalom. Arról is beszélt, hogy informálták róla, Witkoffék Moszkva után Kijevbe utaznak. Szerinte bármi is történjen, az ilyen típusú kapcsolatfelvételek hasznosak. Putyin jelezte készségét arra, hogy tájékoztassa az amerikai felet az ukrajnai konfliktus orosz nézőpontjáról. Donald Trump amerikai elnök különmegbízottja, Steve Witkoff és az elnök veje, Jared Kushner szombaton érkeztek Moszkvába, hogy a háború lezárásáról tárgyaljanak. Peszkov szerint Putyin találkozót tervez velük. Witkoff és Kushner már többször jártak az orosz fővárosban, de vasárnap utaznak először Kijevbe. A CNN arról is írt, hogy Putyin kérte az amerikai delegációt, hogy adják át legjobb kívánságait Trumpnak, aki korábban nagyszerű mediátoroknak nevezte Kushnert és Witkoffot. Trump azt is elmondta a találkozó előtt, jó esélyt lát a megegyezésre. Ugyanakkor orosz tisztviselők szerint kevés a sansz az egyezségre, Moszkva szerint „a helyzet nem Kijev javára változik” a fronton. Fegyvernyugvás a tárgyalásokért Putyin korábban az amerikaiakkal való tárgyalások miatt szünetet rendelt el a Kijev elleni pusztító légicsapásokban, az ukrán fél is így tett Moszkvával. Erről azt mondta, hivatalos csatornákon érkezett kérés erre, az orosz hírszerzés és a külügyminisztérium felé. Szombat reggel óta ezért nem támadták az ukrán fővárost – írja az Interfax . Az orosz elnök hozzátette: „Az ukrán hatóságok felhívást intéztek hozzánk egy tágabb háromnapos tűzszünetért, de mi sosem egyeztünk meg ebben velük.” De szerinte mindent el fognak követni, hogy biztosítsák a tárgyalásokat és a közvetítők épségét. Witkoff meg is köszönte Putyinnak, hogy belement a háromnapos kijevi fegyvernyugvásba, megemlítve, hogy Moszkvát sem fogja ez idő alatt támadás érni. „Ez lehetővé tette, hogy iderepüljünk biztonságban ebben a három napban” – mondta a különmegbízott. Witkoff arról is beszélt az Interfax szerint, hogy tárgyalni tudtak Jurij Usakov elnöki tanácsadóval és Kirill Dmitrijev elnöki különmegbízottal arról, miként lehet a Putyinnal való találkozó „a legjobb és legemlékezetesebb élmény”. Witkoff a családja nevében köszönetet mondott Robert Gilman amerikai tengerészgyalogos elengedéséért is. Kapcsolódó Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Sportscage Riders Sportscage Team Schedules News Trade Dispute Top Stories Sportscage Agriculture Sask Ag Today Weather Polls Win & Events Win Concerts & Events 620 CKRM Country Cookout Shows Gloria Evans Cody Glydon Colin Lovequist Ray Alan Tonya Cherry Podcasts 620 CKRM App Apple App Store Google Play Contact Us Advertise Courtesy of Orano Facebook Saskatchewan’s nuclear capacity takes centre stage in the United Kingdom By SaskToday Sep 5, 2026 | 5:00 PM REGINA, Sask. — Premier Scott Moe is leading a trade and investment mission to the United Kingdom (U.K.) to reinforce Saskatchewan's position as the jurisdiction of choice in nuclear co-operation, states Sask. Trade and Export Development in a press release. Moe will participate in the World Nuclear Symposium and Canada – U.K. Nuclear Day. Minister of Crown Investments Corporation Jeremy Harrison will join the World Nuclear Symposium after representing Saskatchewan at the MSPO Defence Industry Exhibition in Poland alongside federal and provincial counterparts. "Our province has what it takes to be a world leader in nuclear energy development with our extensive uranium resources, nuclear research infrastructure and supply chain capabilities, and Saskatchewan-based businesses and research organizations are at the forefront of the global nuclear renaissance," Moe said. "The U.K. has been a vital gateway to growing Saskatchewan's nuclear sector and I look forward to building on our relationships. After all, it is these relationships that help bring home investment, jobs and reinforce Saskatchewan as a leader in the world's energy future." "Saskatchewan is uniquely positioned to support the next generation of nuclear development around the world," Harrison said. "From our world-class uranium resources to our expertise across the nuclear sector, we have what the world needs. This mission showcases our strengths, deepens relationships with industry and government leaders and creates new opportunities for Saskatchewan's nuclear sector." The World Nuclear Symposium drew more than 1,100 participants from 59 countries in 2025. Moe will be participating in a panel event profiling Saskatchewan's nuclear ecosystem. Canada-U.K. Nuclear Day will feature keynote discussions and expert panels from across the nuclear sector. Moe, alongside Cameco and the Saskatchewan First Nations Centre of Excellence will represent Saskatchewan. Over the past five years, Saskatchewan's exports to the U.K. increased by 177.9 per cent, from $211.5 million in 2021 to $587.6 million in 2025. This growth has been driven by uranium exports, which in 2025 accounted for 57.1 per cent of the province's total U.K. exports. In the same five-year period, the value of exports to Poland have increased by 3,503 per cent, from $2.2 million in 2021 to $79 million in 2025. This growth is mainly due to potash exports. Saskatchewan operates a trade and investment office in London. For more information on Saskatchewan's international network, visit: InvestSK.ca . Tennessee governor Bill Lee has halted the state’s remaining executions for the rest of the year after officials were unable to put Christa Gail Pike to death yesterday. Pike, 50, was alive and loudly snoring after the attempted lethal injection and taken by ambulance from the prison, her attorneys said. She was being treated at a hospital, but they said they hadn’t been told about her condition. She had been scheduled for execution at 10am on Wednesday for the killing she committed at age 18 and would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. https://www.politico.eu/article/spanish-.text: BRUSSELS — A defeat for Pedro Sánchez in Spain’s snap election risks destabilizing the EU by putting the Socialists and Democrats on the back foot in Brussels and pushing them into a more confrontational stance. Sánchez, the only Socialist-aligned leader currently running a large EU country, has provided a center-left counterweight to decisions in a Council largely dominated by the center right. Spain’s lawmakers form the S&D’s largest national delegation in the European Parliament, and when Sánchez strikes a Council deal, Spanish MEPs can usually carry his position through the group, even over internal opposition. A change of government in Madrid would disrupt that arrangement, senior S&D lawmakers told POLITICO. Polls suggest that the country will vote in an administration led by the center-right People’s Party, which would likely partner with the far-right Vox party. Advertisement Advertisement “There might be a temptation to look more critically at Council positions if there is no [longer] a Socialist prime minister of a large country,” said René Repasi, head of Germany’s SPD delegation in Parliament. A second senior S&D lawmaker said Sánchez helped “balance” decisions at the leaders’ table and that his absence would unsettle the informal alliance of the S&D, liberals and the center-right European People’s Party that Commission President Ursula von der Leyen relies on to pass legislation. “If what comes out of the leaders’ table, and the guidelines it gives the Commission, becomes more conservative, it will be less appealing for progressives to feel part of that governing majority,” said the lawmaker, who was granted anonymity to speak about sensitive group matters. The S&D has lost ground elsewhere in Brussels. Since the 2024 European election shifted Parliament to the right, the EPP has passed some legislation with far-right groups. The Socialists have less representation in national governments and fewer commissioners of their own, fueling repeated tensions and attempts to repair the alliance. With Sánchez gone, the last center-left leaders would be Denmark’s Mette Frederiksen and Malta’s Robert Abela — with Magdalena Andersson working to form a government in Sweden. Spain’s election will sound the starting gun a year of consequential votes across major EU countries, including Italy, Poland and France, where the far-right National Rally is leading the polls ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Far-right forces in Brussels are pressing the EPP to drop its ban on cooperating with them and break with its traditional ties to the S&D. Fewer incentives for compromise The S&D, Parliament’s second-largest group, has repeatedly threatened over the past two years to withdraw support for von der Leyen, with some lawmakers urging a more forceful stance on EU policy. Advertisement Advertisement Spain’s Iratxe García, who leads the group, has so far kept Spanish lawmakers in line. She faces a leadership vote on Oct. 21, though she is broadly expected to keep her post. Should Sánchez lose his election, all the S&D’s largest national delegations — from Italy, Romania and France — would be in opposition at home. The only S&D parties still in government would be junior partners in Germany and Austria, alongside Denmark’s Social Democrats, whose hardline stance on migration limits their influence in the group. Without a heavyweight prime minister from a large EU country to keep the S&D in line, von der Leyen would face greater pressure to make more concessions to lawmakers already frustrated by the center-right’s votes with the far right. Iratxe García, who leads the S&D group in the European Parliament and has so far kept Spanish lawmakers in line, holds a press conference in Strasbourg on Feb. 10, 2026. | Magali Cohen/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images “If von der Leyen still delivers on S&D priorities, she will have the support of the group, and if that is not the case, then she will lose the support of the group,” Repasi said. A formal alliance between Spain’s EPP and far-right Vox, he added, “will drive us even more apart.” The S&D would also have fewer “incentives” to compromise without Sánchez’s presence, the second senior lawmaker said, because the group would have less responsibility for maintaining stability in EU institutions. “The institutional responsibility to guarantee support for the Commission and stability in the EU institutions will no longer be there,” the lawmaker said. A tougher line would be easier for the center-left “if the EPP continues striking deals with the far right, and the European Commission fails to offer a politically attractive agenda that progressives can sell to their voters.” Advertisement Advertisement One diplomat called the Socialists’ threat to withdraw support for von der Leyen “not credible,” saying it would isolate the group further: “They just feel a need to send a signal to the EPP.” Weakening or firing von der Leyen also runs against the S&D’s interests, the diplomat added, because the EU has moved further to the right since she first took office and “the next person coming in would be much less inclined to work with them.” Turbulence ahead Brussels is set to become a battleground between Spain’s two main parties, with the Spanish lawmakers leading the Socialists in Parliament, while their rivals in the EPP form that group’s second-largest national delegation. The election is also weighing on talks over the EU’s next seven-year budget, known as the Multiannual Financial Framework, which Brussels aims to conclude by the end of the year. “It’s not going to do any good for the MFF,” a Commission official said, warning that Spain risks dragging its feet during already strained negotiations. The EPP and its allies will try to put debates on Parliament’s agenda to cause discomfort for Sánchez, the official said, likely making the talks more “turbulent.” Spain’s underlying budget position will not change under a new government, a second diplomat said, but “the election will be distracting” and “won’t incentivize finding compromise.” The EPP’s Siegfried Mureșan, Parliament’s lead budget negotiator, warned EU countries not to use the election to delay talks ahead of a leaders’ summit in mid-October. “The European Council shall not use the political situation in Spain as an excuse for further delays.” Advertisement Advertisement EPP leader Manfred Weber declined to comment on what a Sánchez defeat could mean for the Socialists’ influence in Brussels, but voiced support for Spain’s opposition leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo. “Spain’s future is now in the hands of the Spanish people,” he said. “At a time when vision and reform are needed more than ever, the EPP is proud to stand firmly behind Alberto Núñez Feijóo. He has our full support.” Zoya Sheftalovich and Tim Ross contributed reporting.
